dependency: The queue owner treats immediate automatic retry after a failed check as necessary for eventual green status. ATT breaks reliance on that dependency by proposing an initial-attempt-only dispatcher: no failure-triggered re-enqueue, no deferred automatic retry, and no manual repetition of a failed attempt. Zero retries respects the stipulated upper bound; whether disabling automatic re-enqueue is an available experimental control must be confirmed because the enumerated controls do not explicitly list it. Token issuance before an initial full attempt is a separate broker-timing hypothesis, not a retry.

predictions.account: Immediate automatic retry is necessary for eventual green status: the queue owner's necessity hypothesis.
predictions.result: If this account means retry remains indispensable even when every initial attempt receives a token valid throughout its full suite, removing automatic re-enqueue should leave at least one job without a passing check by t=360. Four passing initial attempts would falsify that necessity claim in this case. This prediction is a rival hypothesis, not an observed effect; the supplied predicate provides no additional mechanism supporting it.
predictions.when: After reproducing the supplied baseline, compare otherwise identical refresh-on-dequeue replays with automatic failure re-enqueue enabled and disabled, if the latter control is confirmed available. Keep arrivals, one worker, 40-second suites, 90-second lifetimes, five-second FIFO broker service and t=360 horizon fixed.

predictions.account: Token validity at completion is sufficient; automatic retry is dispensable for the stipulated all-four target.
predictions.result: In the proposed initial-attempt-only replay, request a replacement token only when the FIFO head can claim the free worker; hold that worker idle for the five-second broker service. Requests at t=0,45,90,135 yield issue times 5,50,95,140, worker starts 5,50,95,140, completions 45,90,135,180 and expiries 95,140,185,230. All four strict completion-before-expiry predicates pass with 50 seconds remaining, using four attempts, 160 busy seconds, 20 broker-wait idle seconds and zero retries or failed-attempt service. These are conditional model calculations for an unexecuted intervention, not observed successful futures.
predictions.when: First reproduce the original baseline; next change only token-request timing to refresh on dequeue; then, if available, change only the automatic re-enqueue rule to disabled. Calculate each full replay with expiry processed before equal-time completion and log every issue-time shift.

predictions.account: Repeating an already expired original token cannot recover green status under the stipulated predicate.
predictions.result: With original tokens retained and automatic re-enqueue disabled, the conditional replay ends its four initial suites at t=40,80,120,160: J1 and J2 pass; J3 and J4 fail and are terminal without retries. Passing-job count remains two, while 160 seconds of baseline retry service disappear. Failed-attempt service falls from 240 to 80 seconds, and occupancy after token expiry falls from 230 to 70 seconds. Thus removal alone preserves a partial valued outcome but does not deliver all four passes.
predictions.when: Compare the reproduced original-token baseline with an initial-attempt-only replay changing only failure-triggered re-enqueue, if that control is available; record both terminal failed jobs, zero exhausted retry budgets and no unfinished jobs at t=360.

surviving_outcome: The observed synthetic baseline has two passing jobs and four useless same-token retries. Breaking automatic retry alone conditionally preserves those two full-suite passes and removes the four retry slots; it does not itself achieve all four passes. Combining that break with separately tested on-dequeue token issuance conditionally preserves the complete valued outcome: J1-J4 each pass their sole full 40-second initial attempt by t=180 on one worker, without any automatic, delayed or manual retry. This is a calculated intervention hypothesis, not an observed replay or real release-readiness claim. All four jobs would be finished, none exhausted, and no suite assertion or duration reduced.
unknowns: Disabling automatic failure re-enqueue is not explicitly among the enumerated dispatch controls. Confirm that this dependency-removal control is available; if unavailable, the permitted refresh-on-dequeue calculation still challenges retry necessity by predicting zero failures and zero retry invocations, but a dormant retry rule would not demonstrate that the operating rule itself was removed.
The proposed timing tables and comparisons have not been executed or independently observed. Necessity reasoning and conditional arithmetic do not constitute empirical causal evidence.

The stated retry-wait-expiry return path beyond the fixed baseline remains a hypothesis. The baseline initial failures arise before any retry; the all-initial-pass proposal would not establish whether that feedback loop exists in refresh-enabled workloads with failures.

Intermittent failures, broker outages, representative non-expiry failures, real check durations, credential semantics and operational costs are unavailable or excluded. This case cannot establish a general retry policy or a live deployment recommendation.
